title: Competitive-programming and DSA toolkit
relevance: SDE OAs and CP-style interviews expect overflow-safe arithmetic, bitmask/builtin fluency, STL selection idioms (nth_element, lower_bound, PBDS), and awareness of unordered_map/rand pitfalls that silently WA or TLE.
company_notes: Codeforces and AtCoder GCC judges commonly expose __gnu_pbds and adversarial anti-hash tests; default unordered_map is usually fine on LeetCode-style data but can TLE under Codeforces anti-hash hacks.

phases.goal: Establish the contest boilerplate, integer-width discipline, and basic bit-mask mindset that keep large-input solutions correct and fast.

must_hit.point: Contest fast I/O starts with ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); and printing '\n' instead of endl in hot loops.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites the two sync/tie calls and prefers '\n' because endl flushes.

must_hit.point: On typical platforms int is 32-bit and long long is 64-bit; use long long for products/sums that may exceed about 2^15 per factor or 2^31-1 for totals, and widen before multiply (e.g. 1LL * a[i] * a[j]).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names 32/64-bit widths, when to reach for long long, and early promotion.

must_hit.point: Signed overflow is undefined behaviour — do not rely on wraparound; compute in a wider type (long long, or __int128 for products of two 64-bit values) then cast or take modulo.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States UB for signed overflow and names wider-type / modulo fixes.

must_hit.point: Bitwise ops encode subsets/flags cheaper than vector<bool>; prefer 1LL << k when k may reach 31 or more on a signed 32-bit int, and know set/clear/toggle/test plus x & -x for the lowest set bit.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions subset encoding, 1LL << k caution, and lowest-set-bit idiom.

probes: What boilerplate do you put at the top of main for large contest input, and why avoid endl?
When does n * n blow up in int, and how do you fix overflow safely?

hints.1: Think about stream syncing cost and what happens when a product no longer fits in 32 bits.
hints.2: Name sync_with_stdio/cin.tie, '\n' vs flush, then long long / __int128 before multiply.
hints.3: ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr); prefer '\n'; classic WA is int for n=10^5 products/sums — use long long (or __int128), remembering signed overflow is UB.

phases.goal: Show concrete toolkit mechanics: modular helpers, submasks/builtins/bitset, selection/permutation algorithms, compression/PBDS, custom hashing, and <random>.

must_hit.point: Under a prime MOD (commonly 10^9+7), keep intermediates in [0, MOD) with add/sub normalisation; mul should widen via __int128 (or reduce carefully) because ((a%MOD)*(b%MOD))%MOD is safe only if that product still fits in the multiply type.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions MOD range, negative normalisation, and widen-before-reduce for mul.

must_hit.point: Enumerate non-empty submasks with for (int s = m; s; s = (s - 1) & m); bitmask DP for subsets of n ≤ 20 uses dp[1 << n] with typical O(2^n · n) or O(3^n) passes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the (s-1)&m loop and n ≤ 20 / complexity band for bitmask DP.

must_hit.point: GCC builtins map to CPU instructions: __builtin_popcount(ll), clz/ctz, parity, and __lg; __builtin_clz(0), __builtin_ctz(0), and __lg(0) are undefined — guard x != 0.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names popcount/clz/ctz/parity/__lg and the zero UB trap.

must_hit.point: nth_element is expected linear selection around the k-th element; partial_sort puts the smallest k sorted at the front in O(n log k); next_permutation needs an ascending sort first and costs O(n · n!) total for distinct elements.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates O(n) selection, O(n log k) top-k sorted, and sort+next_permutation enumeration.

must_hit.point: For static data prefer sorted vector + lower_bound/upper_bound; on set/map use member lower_bound (O(log n)) — free std::lower_bound on bidirectional set iterators can degrade to linear; compress coordinates with sort + unique + lower_bound to dense ranks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts vector binary search, member vs free lower_bound on set, and compression recipe.

must_hit.point: GCC __gnu_pbds ordered_set gives find_by_order(k) (0-based k-th) and order_of_key(x) (count strictly < x) in O(log n); for multisets store pair<T,int> with a unique id.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names both order-statistic methods, complexity, and pair trick for duplicates.

must_hit.point: Defeat anti-hash attacks with a strong mix (e.g. SplitmixHash) plus a per-run FIXED_RANDOM seed; replace rand() with mt19937/mt19937_64 + uniform_int_distribution and std::shuffle — RAND_MAX is often only 2^15-1 = 32767 and rand()%n is biased.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties custom seeded hash to mt19937+distribution+shuffle and names RAND_MAX/bias problems.

probes: How do you iterate all submasks of a mask, and when is bitmask DP feasible?
How do you find the k-th element in a dynamic set in O(log n), and why is default unordered_map dangerous on adversarial tests?

hints.1: Think subset-of-bits enumeration and order-statistic trees versus hash tables under attack.
hints.2: Name (s-1)&m, n ≤ 20 DP sizes, PBDS find_by_order/order_of_key, and seeded custom hash or map fallback.
hints.3: Submasks: s=(s-1)&m; bitmask DP for n≤20; PBDS find_by_order/order_of_key in O(log n); SplitmixHash + clock seed or use map; rng = mt19937 + uniform_int_distribution, not rand()%n.

phases.goal: Contrast toolkit choices where speed, portability, and worst-case guarantees diverge.

must_hit.point: bitset<N> is compile-time fixed and word-parallel for &/|/<<; vector<bool> is bit-packed but has proxy-reference weirdness and no bulk bitwise ops between two vectors — for large compile-time N it is often dramatically faster for sieve/reachability/subset DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts fixed bitset algebra vs vector<bool> limitations and when bitset wins.

must_hit.point: Reach for sort when you need full order (O(n log n)), partial_sort for smallest k sorted (O(n log k)), and nth_element when you only need the k-th / partition (O(n)).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the three tools to the three needs with their typical complexities.

must_hit.point: Default unordered_map can degrade to long collision chains and O(n^2) under anti-hash tests; fix with custom hash + random seed, or fall back to map for O(n log n) worst-case — PBDS is GCC-only and not portable to MSVC.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States hash degradation, custom-hash or map remedies, and PBDS portability limit.

must_hit.point: Nested vector<vector<int>> is clear but R separate allocations thrash cache; flat vector of size R*C with g[r*C+c] is contiguous and routinely faster for large grids; std::array when dimensions are compile-time constants.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts clarity vs locality and names flat indexing plus array for fixed dims.

probes: bitset versus vector<bool> — when do you prefer which?
nth_element versus sort versus partial_sort — which do you pick for median vs top-k sorted vs full order?

hints.1: Separate compile-time dense bit algebra from selection algorithms that avoid a full sort.
hints.2: Ask what N being a template argument buys you, and what each algorithm guarantees about order.
hints.3: bitset for fixed N + bulk ops; vector<bool> lacks those; nth_element O(n) for k-th, partial_sort O(n log k) for sorted top-k, sort O(n log n) for full order.

phases.goal: Apply the toolkit under interview/OA pressure: diagnose WA/TLE causes and pick the right tool for the stated need.

must_hit.point: Classic WA: int sum of an array of size n ≤ 10^5 with values up to 10^9, or n * n for n = 10^5 — name the overflow and fix with long long (or modular reduction).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites the n ≤ 10^5 / values-to-10^9 sum or n*n cases and long long/modular fix.

must_hit.point: Answer "count set bits" with __builtin_popcount / popcountll (or Kernighan's x &= x-1 loop) and "lowest set bit" with x & -x; for k-th in a dynamic set mention PBDS find_by_order or a Fenwick/segment tree over compressed coordinates.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives both bit answers and both order-statistic approaches.

must_hit.point: Why not rand()? — small RAND_MAX, poor quality, rand()%n bias; name mt19937 + uniform_int_distribution + std::shuffle, and seed hashes/pivots so adversarial tests cannot force O(n^2).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists RAND_MAX/quality/bias and the mt19937+distribution+shuffle+seed story.

must_hit.point: For a hot R×C grid prefer flat g[r*C+c]; keep nested vectors for clarity or ragged rows; never pass huge grids by value — use references (or a flat vector).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States flat vs nested choice and by-reference / flat to avoid silent deep copies.

probes: Walk a strong CP/DSA C++ interview loop: overflow, bits, lower_bound vs set, nth_element vs sort, unordered_map hashing, rand replacement, nested vs flat grids.
Nested vector versus flat array for a grid — what do you say in an interview?

hints.1: Interviewers want one named failure mode and one concrete snippet per tool.
hints.2: Cover long long overflow, popcount/x&-x, sorted vector lower_bound, nth_element, custom hash or map, mt19937, flat indexing.
hints.3: Overflow→long long; bits→popcount and x&-x; static search→sorted vector; k-th dynamic→PBDS/Fenwick; anti-hash→Splitmix or map; RNG→mt19937 not rand; grids→flat g[r*C+c], pass by reference.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Prefer bitset<N> when N is a compile-time constant and you need fast word-parallel &/|/shifts (sieve, reachability, subset DP). vector<bool> packs bits but has proxy references and no bulk bitwise ops between two vectors; for runtime-sized bitsets use vector<uint64_t> (Boost dynamic_bitset is rarely on judges).
sort for full order at O(n log n); partial_sort when you need the smallest k sorted up front at O(n log k); nth_element when you only need the k-th element / a partition around it at expected O(n).

tradeoffs.topic: sorted vector + lower_bound vs set/map member lower_bound
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For static data a sorted vector plus lower_bound/upper_bound is usually faster and leaner. On set/map use the member lower_bound (O(log n)); free std::lower_bound on set iterators is only bidirectional and may degrade to linear.

Default unordered_map is fine for interviews/most LeetCode tests, but under Codeforces-style anti-hash data it can hit long chains and O(n^2). Use SplitmixHash (or similar) with a per-run random seed, or fall back to map for O(n log n) worst-case.

rand() often has RAND_MAX only 2^15-1, poor quality, and rand()%n bias. Prefer mt19937/mt19937_64 with uniform_int_distribution and std::shuffle; seed from steady_clock and/or random_device so hashes and pivots are not hackable.

tradeoffs.topic: nested vector grid vs flat vector
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Nested vector<vector<int>> is readable but makes R separate allocations and hurts cache. Flat vector of R*C with g[r*C+c] is contiguous and routinely faster for large grids; use std::array when dims are compile-time; keep nested for clarity or ragged rows.

gotchas.trap: Using std::endl in a loop of many lines.
gotchas.correction: endl flushes every time; prefer '\n' and flush only when interactive I/O truly needs it.

gotchas.trap: Relying on signed int wraparound for overflow, or writing int ans = n * n when the product does not fit.
gotchas.correction: Signed overflow is UB. Widen with long long or __int128 before the multiply, then cast or reduce modulo.

gotchas.trap: Mixing signed/unsigned or writing i < v.size() - 1 on an empty vector.
gotchas.correction: size_t underflow and int vs size_t promotions miscompare; prefer signed int/long long indices in CP unless you have a deliberate unsigned/bit-mask reason.
Those are undefined behaviour; always guard with x != 0.
The init type is the accumulator type — pass 0LL (or a long long zero) when the sum may overflow 32 bits.

gotchas.trap: Using free std::lower_bound on a std::set.
gotchas.correction: Prefer set/map member lower_bound for O(log n); free lower_bound on bidirectional iterators may become linear.

gotchas.trap: Shipping PBDS or identity-like unordered_map hashing as if portable/safe everywhere.
gotchas.correction: PBDS is GCC/libstdc++-only (won't compile under MSVC). Default integer hash can be anti-hashed — use a seeded custom hash or map.

gotchas.trap: Sampling with rand() % n or seeding only with time(0).
gotchas.correction: rand()%n is biased when n does not divide RAND_MAX+1; use uniform_int_distribution with mt19937, and seed unpredictably (steady_clock / random_device) once per run.

gotchas.trap: Passing huge vector<vector<int>> grids by value, or storing pointers/references to one shared row.
gotchas.correction: By-value copies every row; pointer aliases make "all rows" change together. Pass by reference (or use a flat vector); vector(R, row) itself copies row safely.
